value.rationale: The new volume-normalized uniform-sampling rule is expressly designed as a practical alternative to volume-sampling projections, yet its nonunit step is unconditionally inferior in expected squared error for any single iteration relative to a unit projection. Noncommutative random-composition dynamics create an exact and nontrivial two-step benefit regime; the determinant-sign formula classifies all row angles, norm ratios and initial-error dependence, including a sharp boundary where no initialization benefits, and provides a rational physical test case. This is a meaningful finite-horizon diagnostic, not a routine reparametrization of the paper’s one-step rate or an unsupported global optimality claim.
